text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- United Nations official in charge of eliminating Iraq's arms of mass destruction Rolf Ekeus to visit Kuwait in November.
- Gulf Arab defence ministers study plan to build "security belt" to protect boarders, Kuwait minister says. The ministers started talks in Riyadh on Tuesday.
- Saudi Arabian security team in Lebanon to investigate bombing of a U.S. military residential complex. In June, 19 Americans were killed in the attack in eastern Saudi Arabia.

- Kuwait's Chamber of Commerce says it did not send team to this week's annual Middle East and North Africa Economic Conference in Egypt. The chamber did not attend the two previous conferences in Amman and Morocco.
- Study says 40 percent of private sector firms in Kuwait prefer foreign labour to employing Kuwaitis.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange Index rises 10.7 points on Tuesday to 1,869.1.
- Teenagers arrested after firing at police patrol.

- United States Air Force Secretary Sheila Widnall says Washington is firm in its resolve to control Iraqi military movements in the air and on the ground. Widnall on Tuesday ended a two-day visit to Kuwait.
